children: IT firms HCL Technologies, Tech Mahindra overtook industry giant Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) in terms of net adds amidst a sectoral pivot towards a productivity-led workforce approach.

In the September-ending quarter, HCL Tech reported 6,440 net adds to its total headcount, followed by Tech Mahindra with 5,446 employees and lastly TCS with 4,258 employees. While much of this growth was fresher-led, experts foresee demand-triggered hiring to become more common, with recruitment surging around major projects and slowing as companies improve utilisation and automate delivery.

“The workforce pyramid is changing with large firms’ impact coming in late. Unlike earlier times when hiring strategy was unidirectional, there are a lot of specific individual ways in which aspirants are hired. Profitability of a project is lot more important now,” said Yugal Joshi, Partner, Everest Group.

He called it a paradoxical or dichotomous approach by companies towards workforce where on the one hand they say AI will do entry level work and they will hire experienced forward deployed engineers but still focus on entry-level hirings to manage spends.
What’s interesting in this quarter is the manner in which companies have adapted their hiring strategy.

title: HCL Technologies, Tech Mahindra overtake TCS in net adds
